THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT 1988,
 AGAINST JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.06.2013, PASSED IN  MVC.NO.36/1990 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND  MACT AT RAIBAG, AWARDING THE COMPENSATION OF RS.97,880/-
 WITH INTEREST AT 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE  DATE OF DEPOSIT & ETC.

JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  ORAL JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 26.06.2013 passed in MVC.no.36/1990 by Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Raibag ('Tribunal', for short), this appeal is filed.

2. Sri M.K. Soudagar, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by insurer (respondent no.3) in claim petition filed by claimant stating that on 07.07.1989 at 7:15 p.m., when he was returning from Ganapathi Temple towards Chikkodi by side of road, driver of tractor bearing registration no.RJE-6645 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against claimant causing accident.
Despite treatment at Dr.Magadum's Hospital for treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act', for short) against driver, owner and insurer of offending tractor.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR 3.

After issuance of notice, petition against respondent no.1 - driver was got dismissed, respondent no.2 was treated as absent and placed ex-parte, respondent no.3 - insurer entered appearance and filed written statement opposing claim petition specifically denying issuance of insurance policy and its coverage as on date of accident apart from contending that driver did not have valid and effective driving licence to drive vehicle as on date of accident.

sentences.text:
2 4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that Kumar Jyoti sustained bodily injures on 07.07.1989 at about 7:15 p.m., near Mahaveer Karate on Raibag-Chincholi road in a tractor accident which was caused due to rash and negligent driving of tractor bearing no.RJE-6645 by its driver respondent no.1?
2. Whether the respondent no.3 proves that the tractor in question was not insured?
3. Whether the petitioner no.1 is entitled for compensation, if so, what is the quantum?
4. What order?
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR 5.
In trial, claimant examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Exhibits-P1 to P15.
No contra evidence was led.

6. On consideration, Tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of tractor by its driver and stating that copy of policy produced by claimant indicated that respondent no.2 was registered owner and respondent no.3 was insurer, held insurer liable to pay compensation as follows:
1

Towards two fracture grievous Rs.60,000/-
injuries 2
Towards medical expenses Rs.2,880/- 3

Towards conveyance, attendant,
nourishment and Mis. Charges Rs.10,000/- etc. 4

Towards loss of future prospectus Rs.27,300/-
Total Rs.97,880/-
7.
Aggrieved thereby, insurer was in appeal.

8. It was submitted, claim petition was filed before District and Sessions Court,
Belgavi in year 1990.
By order dated 08.07.1995, it was transferred to MACT, Athani and by order on 30.10.2010, it was transferred to Court of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Raibag.

entities.text: Court of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Raibag
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It was submitted, after transfer of claim petition from Belgavi to Athani, Tribunal at Athani had issued notice NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR respondent no.2 - owner, which had returned with postal shara as 'party dead 15 years earlier'.

3 9.

sentences.text: Taking note of same, Tribunal had passed order on 16.02.1996 directing claimant to take steps for bringing legal representatives of deceased respondent no.2.
When steps were not taken despite grant of sufficient time, petition came to be dismissed against respondent no.2 on 05.07.2002.
On filing of application, on 29.08.2009 order was recalled and claim petition was restored.
10. Thereafter, instead of bringing legal representatives on record, Tribunal permitted claimant to take out notice by way of paper publication.

Claimant defaulted in following said order, leading to dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2 -
owner once again on 16.07.2010.
But by subsequent order dated 22.09.2010, Tribunal permitted claimant to take out notice to respondent no.2 - owner by way of paper publication.

In meanwhile,
trial commenced and evidence of claimant was recorded.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR 11.

To establish negligence on part of respondent no.1 - driver, claimant relied upon prosecution records and to establish disability and loss of earning capacity, claimant relied upon treatment records and disability certificate.
However on 23.10.2010, claim petition was transferred from MACT, Athani to Tribunal at Raibag and once again notices were issued.
Since order directing notice to respondent no.2 - owner by way of paper publication was not complied, claim petition came to be dismissed for default on 30.04.2013, but restored thereafter.
On 30.05.2013, service by way of paper publication held sufficient and respondent no.2 he was placed ex-parte.

12. Consequently, service of notice on a party who was long earlier reported dead was held sufficient,
said party was placed ex-parte and claim proceeded with!
Further noting absence of panel counsel for appellant - insurance company who had not yet entered appearance, Tribunal held no evidence by insurance company.
13. Specific objection denying issuance of insurance policy though noted, Tribunal overlooked same by referring to an alleged copy of insurance policy furnished by claimant.

But NC:
2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR without any such copy having been marked in evidence.

Thus,
impugned award was not only liable to be set aside on ground that it was passed against dead person, namely owner of insured vehicle and as well as on ground of fastening liability upon insurer without claimant establishing that appellant herein was insurer of vehicle in question, as on date of accident.
On said ground sought for allowing appeal.
14. On other hand, Sri Rajashekhar Burji, learned counsel for respondent no.1 - claimant sought to oppose appeal.

It was submitted, while passing impugned award, tribunal had stated that claimant had produced copy of insurance policy and referring to same rightly fastened liability on insurer and there was no merit in appeal and seeks dismissal.
15. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment, award and record.

sentences.text: From above, it is seen, this appeal is by insurer challenging award not only on ground of award having been passed against dead person, namely owner of offending vehicle but also on ground of ignoring denial of insurance coverage and NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR holding insurer liable claimant producing copy of alleged insurance policy.

Therefore, points that would arise for consideration is:
"1. Whether impugned award passed by Tribunal is liable to be set aside on ground of having been passed against dead person?"
2. Whether impugned award is liable to be set aside for being on account of material irregularity?

Point no.1:
17.
Perusal of order sheet of claim petition would indeed reveal that after claim petition was filed on 06.03.1990, notice was issued and respondent no.2 had remained un-served and placed ex-parte.
After transfer of claim petition from District and Sessions Court, Belagavi to MACT, Athani, fresh notices were issued.

Order sheet dated 16.02.1996 records that notice issued to respondent no.2 had returned with postal shara "addressee had died 15 years back" and therefore, claimant was required to take steps for bringing legal representatives on record.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR 18.
It is also seen that as contended Tribunal had noted death of respondent no.2 and directed claimant to take steps.

But thereafter ignoring said order had permitted claimant to take out notice to respondent no.2 - owner by way of paper publication, treated respondent no.2 has served by said mode, placed him ex-parte and though claimant did not take steps for bringing legal representatives of respondent no.2 nor was there assertion by claimant about respondent no.2 being alive, Tribunal had proceeded to pass award apparently against dead person.
This would be a material irregularity going to root of matter.
19. Besides, insurer in para-7 of its objections, specifically denied and disputed, issuing insurance police to offending vehicle as on date of accident.
Strangely, Tribunal framed issue no.2 placing burden of establishing said fact on insurer.
Further, unlike recorded by Tribunal, copy of insurance policy is not got marked nor even a photocopy of same maintained in record.

Consequently even on ground of fastening of liability on insurer was without claimant establishing appellant as insurer of offending vehicle would also be a material - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3532 HC-KAR irregularity and illegality.
Both of above factors, would go to root of matter rendering award illegal.
Without much ado, point nos.1 and 2 are answered in affirmative.
